newsitem.title: GERMANY: Forsa poll - 71 pct of Germans back EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Forsa poll - 71 pct of Germans back EMU delay.

text.p: Seventy-one percent of Germans surveyed in a new poll backed a delay in the start of Europe's monetary union (EMU) and 45 percent doubted Bonn could meet the Maastricht criteria, Die Woche weekly reported on Thursday.

The survey by the Forsa polling group showed only 21 percent of the 1,002 people queried backed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's firm stand that European Union countries should stick to the the 1999 deadline for EMU to start. The poll was taken between May 30 and June 2.

Only 37 percent thought Germany, one of the prime movers behind the increasingly uphill struggle to launch the euro, could itself meet the Maastricht criteria for membership. The treaty sets a deficit target of three percent of GDP and overall debt of 60 percent of GDP.

Asked whether the powerful Bundesbank should revalue its gold reserves, a key issue in an unprecedented power struggle that saw Bonn back down this week, 57 percent said "no" and only 22 percent said "yes."

Fifty two percent said Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who wanted to force the respected bank to revalue this year and pay him profits to help qualify for the euro, should step down while 35 percent said he should not.
Asked if the Kohl government could solve its economic problems, 71 percent said "no" and only 21 percent said "yes".
